evals.name: carbon-intensity-http
evals.prompt: I want a FiestaBoard plugin that shows the current UK national electricity carbon intensity on my board. There's a free API at https://api.carbonintensity.org.uk/intensity (no key needed) that returns the latest actual gCO2/kWh figure and an index like 'low'/'moderate'/'high'. Build me the plugin. Don't create the GitHub repo or open a registry PR yet — just get it scaffolded, implemented, and passing tests locally.
evals.expected_output: A complete standalone fiestaboard-plugin--carbon-intensity repo: PluginBase subclass fetching from the carbon intensity API, manifest with sensible variables (e.g. intensity value + index), tests that mock requests and pass at >=70% coverage, README + SETUP, ci.yml + release.yml. board-display.png is a placeholder.

evals.name: computing-facts-local
evals.prompt: make me a fiestaboard plugin that displays a random fun fact about computing history along with a little text emoticon (like :-) or \\m/ — remember the board only has a limited character set, no unicode emoji). No external API — just bake in a list of facts and pick one. Scaffold it, implement it, and make sure the tests pass. Don't publish it yet.
evals.expected_output: A complete standalone fiestaboard-plugin--<slug> repo of the 'simple' type (no network). Local list of facts + emoticons, fetch_data picks one, manifest variables match the data keys and demo template, tests pass without mocking any network, README + SETUP, ci.yml + release.yml.

evals.name: nasa-apod-apikey
evals.prompt: build me a FiestaBoard plugin for NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD). It should show the picture's title and a short bit of the explanation text. The API is https://api.nasa.gov/planetary/apod and it needs a NASA API key (I have one). Get it fully set up and tested but hold off on creating the repo or registering it.
evals.expected_output: A complete standalone fiestaboard-plugin--<slug> repo (http type). API key handled via a password-widget setting AND an env_var, read in fetch_data without hardcoding any real key. Manifest variables for title + explanation, tests mock the API and pass, README + SETUP document the key. ci.yml + release.yml present.

evals.name: fitness-oauth-signin
evals.prompt: I want a FiestaBoard plugin that shows today's step count and active minutes from my account on a fitness service called StrideLog. Their API only works with OAuth sign-in (authorization code with PKCE, no client secret needed): authorize at https://stridelog.example.com/oauth/authorize, token at https://stridelog.example.com/oauth/token, scope `activity.read`, and the data is at GET https://api.stridelog.example.com/v1/me/today returning {"steps": 8421, "active_minutes": 47}. Each user will register their own StrideLog app and paste in its client ID. Build it and get the tests passing locally. Don't create the GitHub repo or open a registry PR, and don't try to sign in to anything.
evals.expected_output: A complete standalone fiestaboard-plugin--<slug> repo. manifest.json declares an `oauth` block (relay flow, the two https endpoints, the scope, no client_secret) with fiestaboard_version >=9.5.0 and a client_id settings field. fetch_data calls self.get_oauth_token() on every fetch, returns an unavailable result without making a request when it is None, and sends the token as a Bearer header. The plugin implements no OAuth flow of its own and stores no token. Tests replace get_oauth_token on the instance, mock the API, cover signed-out and 401, and pass. SETUP.md gives the redirect URI https://fiestaboard.app/auth/oauth/redirect. ci.yml pins FiestaBoard to a release with OAuth.
